issues: Finding 9 overstates the prospective-memory evidence by saying that reminder effectiveness depends on cue visibility, confidence, and learned reliability. doi-10-3758-s13421-025-01708-x shows cue visibility and confidence affecting reminder setting/use, not that these variables directly change the effectiveness of a given reminder. doi-10-1186-s41235-019-0195-y likewise shows confidence predicting cognitive offloading. doi-10-3758-s13423-026-02985-6 shows learned reminder reliability changing intention maintenance and vulnerability when expected reminders are absent, rather than establishing a general effect on reminder effectiveness.

Finding 9 also collapses materially different findings about delay into a single unqualified claim. doi-10-3758-bf03201140 reports that, within its tested ranges, reminder-to-target and instruction-to-task delay did not significantly change prospective-memory performance, whereas doi-10-3758-s13421-025-01708-x reports lower prospective-memory accuracy, more reminder use, and larger reminder benefits at longer delays. The studies use different paradigms, so this need not be labeled a direct contradiction, but the synthesis must explicitly preserve the conditional difference instead of stating simply that effectiveness depends on delay.

The contradictions array is empty even though the synthesis contains at least one important cross-paper tension that directly bears on a finding: the differing delay results in doi-10-3758-bf03201140 and doi-10-3758-s13421-025-01708-x. The limitations section discusses an unrelated MMR-versus-temporal-news tension but does not identify or qualify this prospective-memory tension.

Finding 5 is slightly broader than its evidence as written. doi-10-18653-v1-2024-acl-long-390 explicitly supports incremental clustering and summarization as new text arrives. The reduced analysis for doi-10-18653-v1-2026-acl-long-1149 supports chronological report generation, dynamic scheduling, temporal grounding, and efficiency, but does not itself state that the system incrementally processes newly arriving evidence. Referring to plural 'news systems' as incrementally clustering and summarizing therefore risks attributing incremental-stream behavior to both cited news papers.

Gap 8 is correctly left open, but its classification as ENGINEERING is potentially misleading because the stated deficiency is absence of a unified empirical benchmark with independently labeled lifecycle state and longitudinal error measurements. Closing that evidentiary gap would require a new empirical evaluation, not merely documentation or implementation work. This does not invalidate gap completeness, but the classification should be reconsidered if ACADEMIC versus ENGINEERING is intended to distinguish missing evidence from buildable implementation work.
unsupported_claims: The statement in Finding 9 that reminder effectiveness depends on cue visibility and confidence is not directly supported by the cited analyses; those variables are shown to affect reminder use/offloading decisions.

The statement in Finding 9 that reminder effectiveness generally depends on delay is too broad because doi-10-3758-bf03201140 reports no significant delay effect within its tested ranges while doi-10-3758-s13421-025-01708-x reports delay-dependent effects in a different paradigm.

The plural formulation in Finding 5 that 'news systems incrementally cluster and summarize evolving events' is not fully supported by the reduced analysis of doi-10-18653-v1-2026-acl-long-1149; explicit incremental-arrival processing is established by doi-10-18653-v1-2024-acl-long-390.
required_fixes: Rewrite Finding 9 so that reminder-content effects, reminder-setting/offloading determinants, and reliability effects are separated. A faithful formulation would distinguish evidence that target-plus-action reminder content improves prospective-memory performance from evidence that confidence, delay, and cue visibility influence whether people set/use reminders, and from evidence that learned reliability changes internal intention maintenance and failure risk.

Explicitly qualify the delay evidence by naming both doi-10-3758-bf03201140 and doi-10-3758-s13421-025-01708-x and explaining that their results differ under different prospective-memory paradigms and tested delay ranges. Add this as a contradiction/tension or a clearly named scope-qualified inconsistency rather than leaving the contradictions array empty.

Narrow Finding 5 to say that incremental longitudinal summarization is demonstrated by the cited news timeline work and CLIN-SUMM, without implying that every cited chronological-news system is itself incremental in the streaming sense unless that property is supported by its analysis.

Reconsider gap-8 classification. If the pipeline taxonomy defines ACADEMIC as requiring new empirical evidence, classify the missing unified cycle-based benchmark as ACADEMIC; otherwise document why constructing and evaluating such a benchmark is intentionally categorized as ENGINEERING.
notes: All paper_id values used by the synthesis are present in the permitted identifier set, and the stated paper_count of 53 matches the 53 supplied per-paper analyses. The central conclusion is well supported: the corpus contains substantial component-level evidence but no direct end-to-end evaluation of the requested longitudinal cross-thread workplace briefing problem. The eight principal gaps are all kept open, and transfer-domain evidence is generally labeled appropriately rather than being presented as workplace validation. Rejection is driven primarily by a substantive faithfulness/coherence problem in the prospective-memory synthesis: distinct evidence about reminder efficacy, reminder-use decisions, delay, cue visibility, confidence, and learned reliability has been merged into a stronger general causal statement than the analyses support, while a relevant cross-paper tension on delay is omitted from the contradictions treatment. These issues are repairable without changing the synthesis's main conclusion.
